messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a noticeable spike in prefix eviction churn on the canary after the deploy around 12:00. Lots of short-lived ownership flips for small tenants.

oliver: Saw some alerts. Any quick traces? Could be a sequencing/regression.

maya: Pasting a tiny slice of the log I captured:
```
[2026-06-01T12:03:21Z] prefix=tenantA/foo handoff:start owner=op-17 -> op-23
[2026-06-01T12:03:21Z] prefix=tenantA/foo eviction: mark=soft demote_score=0.21
[2026-06-01T12:03:21Z] prefix=tenantA/foo handoff:commit owner=op-23
[2026-06-01T12:03:21Z] prefix=tenantA/foo prefetch: cancelled (owner changed)
```

diego: I did a local bisect and it pointed at PR #3421 — the ownership reshuffle that reordered handoff ack/commit. Hypothesis: optimistic commit moved commit later so demote path can run in between.

sophia: That PR also lowered the demote threshold in the same diff (demote_low 0.25 -> 0.2). Two orthogonal changes but both affect the window where a prefix is considered evictable.

oliver: If handoff-commit is delayed and demote runs, another node might think the key is evictable and claim it, causing flip-flop. That matches the churn pattern.

maya: Repro steps I used locally: synthetic small-prefix traffic (many tiny requests), canary config with `lease_timeout=200ms` and `demote_low=0.2`. Churn shows up in ~20-40s.

diego: Quick mitigation idea: bump `lease_timeout` to 500ms on canary and pause the new ordering change until we confirm. I'll open a tiny revert for ordering only.

sophia: Long-term: we need a clear handoff/demote contract. Options:
- make handoff commit idempotent and visible (handoff-accepted vs handoff-committed)
- add explicit in-flight counter so demote refuses if handoff_inflight > 0
- or move demote to consult a lease-seen timestamp so it can't fire immediately after a handoff start

oliver: I like the in-flight counter + demote refusal as a short-term runtime guard. We'll also need metrics: `prefix.handoff_inflight` and `prefix.demote_attempts` with tags.

maya: I'll try the lease_timeout bump first and report. If churn goes away we have a quick rollback path for prod.

diego: For reproducibility I'm sharing the git bisect steps I used:
```
git bisect start HEAD v1.26
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v1.26
git bisect run ./scripts/evict-smoke.sh
```
Found bad commit: 9f3b2c4 PR #3421
```

oliver: Nice. I'll add a tiny runtime check: if demote triggered and `handoff_inflight(prefix) > 0` then delay demote by jittered backoff 50-200ms and emit metric `demote_delayed_by_handoff`.

sophia: Also add an integration test that simulates delayed `handoff:commit` and verifies no double-ownership in N ms window. That should prevent regressions.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered -> revision 2026-06-01T12:10:00Z (canary/4). Link: https://deploy/revision/2026-06-01T12:10:00Z

maya: I reverted the ordering locally and churn disappears in my smoke runs. Will attach the before/after perf graphs in a follow-up.

diego: Opening revert PR for canary-only: will revert the handoff ordering change and leave demote threshold as-is for now.

oliver: I'll prototype the demote guard and the metrics today; can slip into a hotfix patch if needed.

sophia: I'll author an RFC draft: "Prefix handoff/demote contract" — covering states (started, accepted, committed), idempotency tokens, metrics, and test plan. Ping me to pair-review.

maya: Action items summary (for the thread):
- diego: open revert PR for ordering on canary (in flight)
- oliver: add demote guard + `demote_delayed_by_handoff` metric (PR intent)
- sophia: RFC skeleton + test cases
- maya: run canary with lease_timeout=500ms and report churn numbers

diego: I'll also sticky the bisect logs and the failing commit id in the PR description so it's easy to follow.

oliver: One more: add a lightweight log line `handoff:state=<started|accepted|committed>` with prefix id — that'll help correlate metrics quickly in production audits.

maya: Thanks all — keep updates here. :eyes:
